title: The Crossing
logline: Where the stream has no bridge, people cross by a rope tied to a tree: a run-up, a grip, a swing, an unsteady landing, and then, every time, a moment of standing firm on the far side.

object.note: Object 10 (identity not chosen) may appear subtly, for example among Chathura's things while he travels, waits or watches, only where it sits naturally in a real moment. Never staged, never the subject.

thread_in.thread: From knowing without stopping to think to a single act of letting go: a stream with no bridge, a rope tied to a tree, and the moment of standing firm on the far side.

thread_out.thread: One crossing becomes many: a ferryman's same short lagoon crossing in stillness and in chop, reaching the same bank by a different way each time.

requirements: A real village where a bridgeless crossing is part of daily life
Consent from the community and anyone filmed crossing
Safety oversight; the crew must never encourage a risky crossing

suggestions.name: A hill-country or wet-zone village with a seasonal stream crossing
suggestions.why: Bridgeless stream crossings by rope, log or pole are still part of daily life in some hill-country villages.
suggestions.verify: A specific village and crossing must be identified and confirmed safe to film.

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed.
